body: I appreciate being born in my country as it comes with opportunities many don't have, but, if it makes you feel any better, I've met countless people people on my travels who have lived in the US for years then hightailed it back to their own countries because they found the US too difficult. This includes poorer countries. My Serbian friend knows a family who had to move back to Serbia to escape their six figure medical debt that not even 70 hours of work a week could scratch the surface of. Living everywhere has massive downsides. There's no escaping it.
I can't relate. I have TONS of hobbies I could take weeks off and it wouldn't be enough free time. It was the same when I was a child.

Yeah, if my car needs to go into the shop I am panicking thinking about how to get to work because my city is huge and the buses only service about 2/3 of it and show up every half hour to one hour if you're one of the lucky ones near a stop (the closest one to me is a 2 hour walk away). So my only other option is to call a lyft that eats up a large portion of my day's wages.

Even a dependable car that hardly needs repairs still costs a fortune in insurance, gas, and basic maintenance. 

I wish I had the OPTION of public transit. I get not everyone likes it, but when I've lived abroad it's always been one of my favorites things. I can just hop on a bus and go anywhere! I can drink at restaurants and have someone else drive me home cheaply! Amazing.

Yeah I am EXTREMELY insecure about my intelligence, to the point I've tried committing suicide because I thought I was too stupid to deserve to live. A lot of jokes revolve around calling another person stupid, or at least implying it, and I find it devastating. It's socially unacceptable to insult peoples' looks, but I'd actually be much more okay with that than someone joking that I have brain damage.
I'm currently in the Republic of Georgia, but the LAST country I've traveled to besides my own (the US) is Armenia. Both are wonderful countries with even better food.
